spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
# Slop Audit: Marin, Levanter, Haliax, and Tests

Audit date: 2026-06-16  
Commit reviewed: [`000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f)  
Scope: `lib/marin`, `lib/levanter`, `lib/haliax`, and all `tests`, excluding `experiments` implementation files. Tests that import `experiments` were still reviewed because the request included all tests.

## Taxonomy

| ID | Slop Type | Signal | Why It Is Negative |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | Behaviorless tests | No assertion or only "does not raise" smoke coverage. | The test can pass while the behavior is wrong, and often only proves that imports/config wiring happened once. |
| S2 | Tautological tests | `isinstance`, registry membership, constructor/default checks, `is not None`, "method exists". | These mostly prove Python, dataclasses, or global registration, not user-visible behavior. |
| S3 | Implementation-pinned tests | Assertions on `_private` fields/helpers, call counts, internal dispatch, exact helper order. | They fail under harmless refactors and miss externally visible regressions. |
| S4 | Brittle timing/infrastructure tests | `time.sleep`, real network/GCS/HF dependencies in unit-shaped tests, manual benchmark tests. | They are flaky, slow, skipped in CI, or environment-dependent instead of behavior-dependent. |
| S5 | Permanent skip graveyard | `@pytest.mark.skip` without a path to re-enable. | Dead tests look like coverage while providing none. This is explicitly rejected by `TESTING.md`. |
| S6 | Swallowed failure paths | Broad `except Exception: pass`, `return None`, or `return False` with little/no context. | Real bugs become silent fallbacks; operators lose the cause of production failures. |
| S7 | Assert-as-validation | `assert` used for runtime input validation or externally reachable errors. | Assertions disappear under optimized Python and conflate invariants with user/config errors. |
| S8 | Weak boundary contracts | Tests mock inside the system instead of using a fake boundary or persisted state. | They verify wiring rather than effects and tend to bless the current implementation shape. |

Severity rubric:

| Rating | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| High | Masks real failures, creates false confidence in critical code, or removes coverage entirely. |
| Medium | Brittle or low-value enough to slow refactors and reviews, but some behavior signal remains. |
| Low | Local cleanup; not harmful alone, but part of a repeated pattern. |

## Findings

### 1. Permanent skipped tests and manual benchmarks are acting as fake coverage

Rating: High  
Taxonomy: S4, S5

Representative sources:

- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_train_asr.py:16`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_train_asr.py#L16)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/whisper_test.py:28`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/whisper_test.py#L28)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_attention.py:64`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_attention.py#L64)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_audio.py:57`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_audio.py#L57) and [`test_audio.py:110`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_audio.py#L110)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_hf_gpt2_serialize.py:50`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_hf_gpt2_serialize.py#L50)
- [`tests/rl/test_weight_transfer.py:293`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/rl/test_weight_transfer.py#L293) and [`test_weight_transfer.py:377`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/rl/test_weight_transfer.py#L377)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_gdn_kernels.py:471`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_gdn_kernels.py#L471)

These are not normal conditional skips such as optional-dependency or backend gating. Several are permanently disabled with TODO/flaky/gone-file reasons, or are benchmark/manual tests checked into pytest collection. Delete them, move manual benchmarks out of pytest, or mark them with a real runnable condition plus behavior assertions.

### 2. Large smoke tests have no behavioral contract

Rating: High for training/export entrypoints; Medium for tracker wrappers  
Taxonomy: S1, S6

Representative sources:

- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_train_lm.py:31`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_train_lm.py#L31)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_train_lm.py:57`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_train_lm.py#L57)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_viz_lm.py:19`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_viz_lm.py#L19)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_export_to_hf.py:23`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_export_to_hf.py#L23)
- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_trackio.py:15`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_trackio.py#L15)
- [`tests/vllm/test_llm_inference.py:33`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/vllm/test_llm_inference.py#L33)

The comments say "just testing if ... has a pulse"; the tests then run expensive code without checking a stable effect. Some also swallow cleanup failures with `except Exception: pass`. Better contracts would check checkpoint files, exported HF config/loadability, generated visualization artifacts, logged records, or a small structured result.

### 3. Private representation tests are overfitting current internals

The artifact registry checks similarly assert `_root` rather than behavior through a public property or lookup. If the representation is truly part of the contract, expose a named public inspection API; otherwise test public behavior.

### 4. Registry and type-only tests provide weak signal

Rating: Medium  
Taxonomy: S2

Representative sources:

- [`tests/evals/test_structured_evals.py:7`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/evals/test_structured_evals.py#L7)

Prefer a tiny end-to-end decode/stage/run through the public boundary, or collapse these into one explicit schema/config contract test with stronger assertions.

### 5. Mock-dispatch tests verify helper wiring instead of effects

Rating: Medium  
Taxonomy: S3, S8

Representative sources:

- [`lib/levanter/tests/test_tokenizers.py:1474`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/levanter/tests/test_tokenizers.py#L1474)

The tokenizer staging tests are the clearest cases: several assertions are `assert_not_called()` / `assert_called_once()` on private staging helpers. They should assert final staged files, cache reuse, corrupt mirror recovery, and no network boundary hit through a fake external boundary. Some kernel dispatch tests do assert output/warnings too, so they are less bad, but the call-count assertions should remain secondary to observable fallback behavior.

### 6. Sleep-based tests encode timing races

Rating: Medium  
Taxonomy: S4

Representative sources:

- [`tests/rl/test_replay_buffer.py:140`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/rl/test_replay_buffer.py#L140)

Root `TESTING.md` says not to use `time.sleep()` in tests. Use fake clocks, injected timestamp sources, poll-with-deadline helpers, or event synchronization. `test_rollout_storage` is especially fixable: timestamp ordering can use an injected `now` or explicit sortable metadata instead of sleeping 10ms.

### 7. Runtime validation uses `assert`

Rating: High  
Taxonomy: S7

Representative sources:

- [`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/inference_ctx/render.py:202`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/inference_ctx/render.py#L202)

These are externally reachable renderer/tokenizer conditions, not internal proofs. Under `python -O`, they disappear. Replace them with explicit `ValueError`/domain exceptions carrying the role/model/tokenizer context.

### 8. Best-effort production paths swallow broad failures

Rating: Medium to High depending on path  
Taxonomy: S6

Representative sources:

- [`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/rollout_worker.py:617`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/rollout_worker.py#L617)

- [`lib/marin/src/marin/transform/conversation/transform_conversation.py:111`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/marin/src/marin/transform/conversation/transform_conversation.py#L111)

- [`lib/marin/src/marin/execution/executor.py:318`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/executor.py#L318)

Some of these are intentionally best-effort, but the implementation pattern is still sloppy: broad catches with no structured signal. Catch expected exception types, log at debug/warning with context, increment a metric when applicable, and keep the fallback explicit. For parser normalization, decide whether invalid JSON arguments should remain raw, become an error, or be tagged as unparsed.

### 9. Real-service and hard-coded-path tests blur unit/integration boundaries

Rating: Medium  
Taxonomy: S4

Representative sources:

- [`tests/vllm/test_llm_inference.py:35`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/vllm/test_llm_inference.py#L35)
- [`tests/rl/test_checkpoint_transfer.py:20`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/rl/test_checkpoint_transfer.py#L20)
- [`tests/rl/test_checkpoint_transfer.py:28`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/rl/test_checkpoint_transfer.py#L28)
- [`tests/rl/test_rl_experiment_utils.py:158`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/000aff1b3894df6ae78642b0e71c49a020aecd8f/tests/rl/test_rl_experiment_utils.py#L158)

Tests with real GCS model paths, CI-wide skips, or TPU-only service assumptions should be clearly integration-marked and separated from unit tests. Where possible, use temp fsspec filesystems or existing fakes to check path reconstruction and region behavior.

## Not Flagged Despite Pattern Matches

- `np.testing.*` assertions were initially detected as "no assert" by AST because they are function calls. I treated those as real assertions.
- Exact string checks in data rendering tests often are real contracts because downstream readers consume rendered text/JSONL. I did not flag those unless they were only incidental logs/messages.
- Some background/concurrency tests use private helpers such as `_wait_until_idle`; those still assert observable forwarded logs/artifacts, so I did not treat the helper use alone as a finding. The private queue/drop counter assertion is weaker but not as severe as the representation-pinned tests.

## Recommended Cleanup Order

1. Delete or re-home permanent skips/manual benchmarks. This removes fake coverage quickly.
2. Add explicit artifacts/output assertions to Levanter entrypoint smoke tests (`train_lm`, `viz_lm`, export, Trackio).
3. Replace `assert` runtime validation in Marin renderers with explicit exceptions and tests for those exceptions.
4. Refactor the highest-churn private representation tests (`NamedRef`, artifact registry) toward public behavior contracts.
5. Replace sleep-based RL/storage tests with fake clocks or poll/event synchronization.
6. Narrow broad production catches and add structured logging/metrics for intentional best-effort fallbacks.

## Scan Method

I reviewed repository guidance (`AGENTS.md`, `TESTING.md`, and subproject `AGENTS.md` files), then scanned 824 Python files in scope with `rg` and an AST probe for:

- no-assert test functions,
- `isinstance`/`hasattr`/`is None`/`is not None` assertions,
- private attribute assertions,
- mock call assertions,
- broad `pytest.raises`,
- `time.sleep`,
- `pytest.mark.skip`,
- broad `except` handlers that pass or return sentinel values,
- hard-coded `gs://marin...` paths and environment-dependent test setup.

I manually inspected representative hits before assigning ratings.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
Our current grug/pipeline examples all require the user to initiate them via the `uv run iris` command line. This introduces an easy place to accumulate errors:

* Should the user have passed a reservation, but forgot?
* Did they ask for resources the script didn't need, thinking it needed to run the launcher on a TPU
* Did they put it in the wrong region?

This adds up to wasted time and energy. Let's adjust all of our boot scripts to instead hoist the Iris client themselves, and incorporate any CLI options _they_ want to specify e.g. region, or TPU type. We can apply a common pattern, but we don't need a marin launcher library or anything.

Let's add a warning if they are run and e.g. `iris.job_info()` is not None: this indicates the user accidentally ran them from the `uv run iris` command instead of directly.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read AGENTS.md + fix-issue/commit skills
- [x] Actionability check — actionable (clear definition of done)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight — no open PR/issue
- [x] Research current launch pattern + Iris client SDK
- [x] Scope assessment — multi-script design change (>100 LOC, multi-module) → analysis, not PR
- [ ] Human review of proposed approach before implementation

# Research

Boot scripts (`experiments/grug/*`, `experiments/tutorials/*`, ~13 files) end with an `if __name__ == "__main__"` block that calls a submit helper relying on `current_client()`. `current_client()` only reaches the cluster when the script is *already inside* an Iris task — i.e. when launched via `uv run iris --cluster=marin job run -- python -m experiments.grug.base.launch`. Run plainly (`python launch.py`) it silently falls back to `LocalClient`. So the cluster/region/resources/extras live in the hand-typed `iris job run` line, not in the script — exactly the error surface the issue calls out (forgotten reservation, wrong region, over-requested launcher resources).

All the machinery to connect from a dev box (resolve cluster name → config → controller discovery → tunnel → stored token → `IrisClient`) already exists, but it is embedded in the **click CLI**, not exposed as a callable SDK entry point. Making scripts self-running means extracting that into a reusable helper and rewriting every boot script's `__main__`.

**Relevant code**
- [`experiments/grug/base/launch.py#L251-L252`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/base/launch.py#L251-L252) — current `__main__`, no client hoist
- [`experiments/defaults.py#L375-L408`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/defaults.py#L375-L408) — `_submit_train_job` → `current_client()`
- [`experiments/grug/dispatch.py#L42-L62`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/dispatch.py#L42-L62) — closest existing direct-submit pattern
- [`lib/iris/src/iris/cli/connect.py#L83-L129`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/connect.py#L83-L129) — controller discovery + tunnel (to extract)
- [`lib/iris/src/iris/cli/main.py#L112-L155`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/main.py#L112-L155) — cluster→config + token resolution
- [`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/client/job_info.py#L85`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/client/job_info.py#L85) — `get_job_info()` for the misuse warning

# Proposed Approach (design change — review before implementation)

Multi-module and >100 LOC, so flagging for review rather than opening a PR.

**1. Expose connection as an SDK helper (no new "launcher library").** Extract the non-click parts of `connect.py`/`main.py` into a callable, e.g. `iris.client.connect_cluster(cluster: str, *, timeout_ms=...) -> IrisClient` that resolves the cluster config via `resolve_cluster_config`, discovers the controller, establishes the tunnel (returned as a context manager so it closes cleanly), loads the stored `iris login` token, and returns a connected `IrisClient`. The CLI then calls the same helper, so there is one connection path, not two.

**2. Add a small shared `__main__` helper for experiments** (e.g. `experiments/launch.py` or extend `experiments/defaults.py`) that:
   - parses CLI options with the repo's existing `draccus` pattern: `--cluster` (default `marin`), `--region`, `--tpu-type` — overriding the script's `ResourceConfig`/region instead of requiring an `iris job run` line;
   - **warns on misuse**: if `get_job_info() is not None`, the script was launched *via* `uv run iris` (double-wrapping) — log a prominent warning per the issue (open question below: warn-and-continue vs hard-fail);
   - hoists the client via `connect_cluster(...)`, sets it as the current Fray client (`set_current_client`), then runs the script's existing submit path unchanged (`_submit_train_job`/`dispatch_grug_training_run` already go through `current_client()`).

**3. Convert the ~13 boot scripts** to call this helper from `__main__`, and update `experiments/grug/README.md` + tutorial docs to drop the `uv run iris job run` invocation in favor of `uv run python experiments/grug/base/launch.py --cluster=marin --tpu-type=v5p-8`.

**Open questions for a human**
- Where should the extracted connection helper live — `iris.client` (preferred; keeps cluster-resolution in Iris) vs `fray`?
- On accidental in-job execution (`get_job_info() is not None`): warn-and-continue, or hard-fail? The issue says "add a warning," so warn-and-continue unless you prefer a fail.
- Resources today come from each script's `ResourceConfig` (e.g. `ResourceConfig.with_tpu("v5p-8")`). `--tpu-type`/`--region` should override these — confirm precedence (CLI > script default).

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body: A series of experiments on the [Leonardo](https://www.hpc.cineca.it/systems/hardware/leonardo/) cluster plumbing [MarinSkyRL](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL). Aim is to optimize throughput for *non-agentic* tasks ... Leonardo is in principle viable for agentic rollouts as well, but because of the rotating keys, no-internet-on-compute-node limitation and limited VRAM per node (A100 64GB) it is expected that Jupiter, MareNostrum, EmpireAI and potentially Iris TPU will be preferred for agentic.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
## Leonardo non-agentic RL throughput results — gsm8k GRPO (short) + MATH (long-CoT)

Results from the MarinSkyRL throughput ablations on Leonardo. Methodology is "measure the per-step timing breakdown from the run logs, sweep one knob at a time, compare on **effective tokens/s** for work-changing cells and **sec/step** for work-fixed cells."

### Constraints & hparams

**Hardware / stack**
- CINECA Leonardo, **A100-64GB** (4/node; NVLink intra-node, InfiniBand inter-node). 64 GB/GPU is the binding VRAM limit; no compute-node internet; rotating keys.
- MarinSkyRL (`skyrl-train`): FSDP2 policy + vLLM rollout, **`colocate_all=true`**, `run_engines_locally=true`, NCCL policy→engine weight sync, `use_kl_loss=false`. Synchronous path (gen and train do **not** overlap).

**gsm8k grid base** — Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, GRPO. Canary: `train_batch_size=32` · `n_samples_per_prompt=4` · `gpu_memory_utilization=0.70` · `enforce_eager=true` · 4 engines × TP1 · `micro_*_batch_size_per_gpu=8` · `max_generate_length=512`. Reference: **9.58 s/step** (233-step epoch).

**MATH (long-CoT) base** — Hendrycks MATH L3–5 (5,582 train) + MATH-500 val; Minerva boxed-answer **±1 reward**; `train_batch_size=64` · `n_samples=4` · `max_generate_length=4096` · CUDA graphs ON. Natural CoT (~600–660 tok), no forced EOS.

**Protocol** — 25-step runs; warm-mean over steps 6–25 (first 5 discarded). Reward is *not* converged at 25 steps, so **entropy stability** (~0.36, no collapse everywhere) is the correctness guard, not absolute reward.

### gsm8k 1.5B throughput grid (18 cells)

- **CUDA graphs (`enforce_eager=false`) is the standout near-free win: −29% sec/step (9.61 → 6.81), generation −50% (5.73 → 2.89 s).** Should be ON always.
- **Wider rollout batch (`train_batch_size` × `n_samples`) scales effective tokens/s** by filling the otherwise-starved generator. Best balance: `combo_C` (tbs128·n8·gmu0.85·cudagraph·micro16) = **12,882 eff tok/s @ 20.7 s/step**. Max throughput: `max_width` (tbs512…) = **15,231 eff tok/s** but 70.7 s/step.
- **The bottleneck MIGRATES with width.** At base width the canary is **generation-bound (gen 60%) AND the generator is starved** (KV cache usage 0.0–0.3%, "Running" 1–6 of a 1.3M-token cache). Beyond ~tbs128, **`policy_train` compute becomes the wall** (tbs256 50%, combo_D 56%, max_width 58%) while generation stays ~6–16 s and KV stays <11%. It is **never memory-bound** (max_width peaked 10.2% KV; the only "ceiling" was *dataset exhaustion* — epochs=1 × 7,473 rows ÷ tbs512 = 14 steps).
- **Layout:** 4×TP1 > 2×TP2 > 1×TP4 for the 1.5B; colocated > disaggregated at 4 GPU.

### Multi-node generator scaling (batch fixed at 2,048 seqs; scale engines = 4×nodes)

| nodes | engines | sec/step | gen-frac | policy_train-frac | sync_weights s | eff tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 36.9 | 24.3% | 55.7% | 1.05 | 14,435 |
| 2 | 8 | 73.7 | 8.6% | 68.4% | 2.40 | 7,222 |
| 4 | 16 | 46.6 | 10.5% | 62.1% | 3.63 | 11,394 |
| 8 | 32 | 35.9 | 12.3% | 51.1% | 6.33 | 14,838 |

**gsm8k/1.5B is never generation-bound — zero extra engines help.** 1→2 nodes is a sharp regression (cross-node FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter on a tiny 1.5B doesn't amortize); 8 nodes only *breaks even* with 1 node. New monotonic limiter at scale = `sync_weights` (NCCL broadcast grows with engine count).

### Model-size saturation on a real long-CoT task (MATH), single node 4×A100-64GB

| model | parallelism | sec/step | gen-frac | policy_train-frac | avg gen tok | reward (±1) | OOM? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.5B | FSDP4 + 4×TP1 | 28.3 | **0.52** | 0.35 | 609 | −0.95 (~2% pass) | ok |
| 3B | FSDP4 + 4×TP1 | 41.7 | 0.47 | 0.40 | 663 | −0.81 | ok |
| 7B | FSDP4 + 4×TP1 | 68.4 | 0.45 | 0.42 | 659 | −0.13 | ok |
| 14B | FSDP4 + 2×TP2 | 100.9 | **0.32** | **0.53** | 612 | ~0.00 (~50% pass) | ok |
| 32B | FSDP4 + 1×TP4 | — | — | — | — | — | **OOM ceiling** |

- **Direction flip vs the naive guess:** on a real long-CoT task the **small end is generation-bound** (1.5B gen-frac 0.52) — opposite of short-gsm8k. As size grows the system becomes **more train-bound** (FSDP fwd+bwd scales superlinearly with params); **crossover is 7B↔14B**.
- Reward rises monotonically with size (~2% → ~50% MATH pass). **32B OOMs single-node** (cleared vLLM init but OOM'd in the FSDP backward) → needs multi-node / disaggregated.

### Bigger models, multi-node (MATH)
- **Qwen3-32B (dense): TRAINS on 2 nodes / 8 GPU** — FSDP (cpu_offload + gradient_checkpointing), vLLM 4×TP2 (TP1 OOMs), gmu 0.75, `max_model_len=8192`. ~1,534 s/step, **policy_train 71%** (gen-frac **0.19** — the train-bound trend continues: 1.5B 0.52 → 14B 0.32 → 32B 0.19).
- **Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE):** EP trainer path works end-to-end (grouped-GEMM + router-replay; `torchtitan` installed, zero stack conflict), but OOMs at the colocated full-weight `broadcast_to_inference_engines` → also needs multi-node / disaggregated weight-sync.

### Context-length stress (Qwen2.5-7B; workload fixed at prompt 1024 / gen 4096; only `max_model_len` grows)

| max_model_len | vLLM max-concurrency | sec/step | gen-frac | KV% pk | OOM? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16k | 38.9× | 68.6 | 0.46 | 4.2 | ok |
| 32k | 19.5× | 71.4 | 0.47 | 4.1 | ok |
| 65k | 9.7× | 69.8 | 0.47 | 4.2 | ok |
| 131k | 4.9× | 70.5 | 0.47 | 4.1 | ok |

**No context ceiling to 131k on 4×A100-64GB** (KV pool constant ~638k tok / 34 GiB @ gmu 0.85; max-concurrency halves cleanly per doubling; throughput flat ~70 s/step). **Caveat:** this is a KV-*capacity* test — the ~660-tok CoT never fills the window; a true long-context test needs a long-**input** task (repo-level / long-doc), where realized concurrency would collapse toward ~1 and the actual ceiling would appear.

### Takeaways for Leonardo non-agentic RL
1. **Single-node throughput recipe:** `enforce_eager=false` + `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85` + wide batch (tbs128–256 × n8) + `micro_train_batch_size_per_gpu=16` → ~13–15k eff tok/s at 1.5B. (Raise `epochs` for wide-tbs so runs aren't capped by dataset exhaustion.)
2. **Generation-boundedness is a function of (model size, CoT length), not batch alone:** small models + long CoT → generation dominates (added generators pay off); large models / short outputs → train-bound (levers are train-side micro-batch/sharding + the structural **fully-async** overlap, which is the biggest untapped win and not yet exploited here).
3. **64 GB/GPU is the real ceiling** for ≥32B colocated long-context RL → multi-node / disaggregated (offload inference off the training GPUs).

## OPD grid results — on-policy distillation (Qwen3-32B teacher → Qwen3-1.7B student), gsm8k, Leonardo

Companion to the pure-RL throughput grid above. **OPD** = on-policy distillation: the student (Qwen3-1.7B) generates rollouts via vLLM; per-token reward = −KL(student‖teacher) over the student's own tokens (`advantage_estimator=no_op`, `policy_loss_type=importance_sampling`, `use_kl_in_reward=true`). FSDP ref worker = KL teacher; a separate vLLM-served **Qwen3-32B** supplies top-K logprobs. No env reward. Non-agentic, local gsm8k parquet. Base: 2 nodes × 4 A100-64GB, teacher TP2 + student 1.7B FSDP2 + 4× colocated vLLM TP1.

**Structural finding:** OPD is **teacher-score-bound — 90–97% of every step** is the 32B teacher scoring rollout tokens (`prompt_logprobs=top_k` over every response token). Student generate (8–24 s) and train (38–91 s) are noise. So the speed levers all act on teacher scoring; convergence is governed separately by lr.

### Batch 1 — speed (one knob off base; warm-mean steps 5–15)
| cell | knob vs base | sec/step | teacher-score % | KL Δ (run) | note |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **base** | topk128·lr1e-5·tbs64·n8·gen1024·TP2·eager | 1461 | 95.7% | −0.022 | reference |
| **topk32** | top_k=32 | **532** | 89.5% | −0.023 | **2.74× faster, KL-Δ unharmed** |
| topk64 | top_k=64 | 834 | 93.0% | **−0.028** | best Batch-1 KL-Δ |
| topk256 | top_k=256 | 2663 | 97.3% | −0.018 | 1.82× slower, *worst* total Δ |
| teacherTP4 | teacher TP4 | 1401 | 95.5% | −0.026 | ≈ base — teacher scoring not TP-bound (non-lever) |
| tbs128 | train_batch=128 | 2899 | 95.9% | −0.030 | ~2× tokens → ~2× wall; eff tok/s flat (anti-lever) |
| gen512 | max_gen=512 | 796 | 93.9% | −0.036 | −46% step (halves scored tokens); diff operating point |
| cudagraph | enforce_eager=false | 1446 | 95.8% | −0.027 | no win (student gen <2% of step) |

**top_k is THE speed knob** (superlinear: each doubling ≈1.6–1.85× cost) **and convergence does not scale with it** — k=32–64 captures the bulk of teacher mass for this pair, so cheap top_k loses ~nothing in KL descent. teacherTP4 / cudagraph are non-levers here; tbs128 is anti. Entropy healthy everywhere (0.18→0.29–0.35, no collapse).

### Batch 2 — convergence (one knob off base; 8h wall ≈16 steps)
| cell | lr | n_samp | steps | KL first→last (Δ) | pass@k last | sec/step | note |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|--:|---|
| lr3e6 | 3e-6 | 8 | 16 | 0.357→0.337 (−0.020) | p@8 **0.03** | 1428 | lr too low — no task learning (≈ base lr1e-5) |
| **lr3e5** | 3e-5 | 8 | 16 | 0.357→0.313 (**−0.043**) | p@8 **0.75** | 1417 | **WINNER** — pass@8 0.03→0.75; entropy/grad healthy |
| lr1e4 | 1e-4 | 8 | 16 | 0.357→**5.59** (+5.23) | p@8 0.39 | 1415 | **diverges** (KL spike 19, grad 21) — too aggressive |
| n4 | 1e-5 | 4 | 16 | 0.366→0.334 (−0.031) | p@4 0.34 | **723** | cheapest (2× steps/hr), higher-variance, still descends |
| n16 | 1e-5 | 16 | 10/12 ⛔TIMEOUT | 0.360→0.343 (−0.017) | p@16 0.59 | 2843 | lowest-variance; killed by 8h wall (partial accepted) |

**lr — not top_k — is the dominant convergence lever; knee at lr=3e-5.** Batch-1's flat KL descent + stuck pass@8 (~0.03) was an lr=1e-5 artifact: at lr=3e-5 the *same* config doubles KL-Δ and lifts gsm8k pass@8 0.03→0.75 (first cell to actually learn the task). lr=3e-6 ≈ no movement; lr=1e-4 diverges. lr and top_k are **orthogonal** (lr = whether it converges; top_k = teacher-mass fidelity per second).

### combo_opt — confirmation (`lr=3e-5 · top_k=64 · n8 · gen1024`, 16 steps)
- **pass@8 0.75–0.78** — matches the lr3e-5 winner (full convergence)
- **KL Δ ≈ −0.05** — best clean KL-Δ of the whole grid
- **832 s/step — ~1.7× faster** than the lr3e-5 cell (topk128, 1417 s/step), entropy healthy 0.30

Confirms orthogonality: top_k=64 keeps lr3e-5's convergence at 1.7× the speed.

### Recommended production OPD config (grid closed 2026-06-07)
**`lr=3e-5 · top_k=64 · n_samples=8 · gen=1024 · teacher TP2 · cudagraph off`** → gsm8k pass@8 ~0.75–0.78, KL-Δ ~−0.05, ~832 s/step (2 nodes / 8×A100). lr is the dominant convergence lever (knee at 3e-5), top_k=32–64 the cheap near-lossless speed lever, n_samples a clean speed×variance trade.

## Analysis — best RL vs best OPD (RESOLVED by the cross-grids)

> **Updated 2026-06-08.** This supersedes the original "RL has only a throughput result, the comparison is still owed" framing. The two cross-grids — [RL accuracy + OPD throughput](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6218#issuecomment-4647852428) — have now run, so the head-to-head is no longer owed; it's answered.

**Verdict (gsm8k, ~1.5–1.7B student): pure RL beats OPD on accuracy *and* on compute-to-accuracy.**

| | accuracy (pass@8) | speed | converges in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **RL** — combo_acc(_stab), lr1e-5+n8+gen1024 | **~0.95–0.97** (≈task ceiling) | ~24–50 s/step | ~80–380 steps |
| **RL** — `base_q3`, **matched Qwen3-1.7B**, lr1e-6 | **0.94 peak** / 0.81 final | ~34 s/step | ~260 steps |
| **OPD** — base / topk16 (Qwen3-1.7B ← 32B) | ~0.82–0.83 (top3) | 836 → **387** s/step | ~16 steps |

On the **same student (Qwen3-1.7B), same task**, RL reaches **~0.94+** vs OPD's **~0.82**, while running **~10–20× cheaper per step** (≈19–50 s vs 387–836 s) — RL does ~40–70× more steps/hr. So both the accuracy ceiling and the pass@8-per-GPU-hour axis go to RL here.

**Why OPD loses the ceiling:** OPD distills toward the **Qwen3-32B teacher's distribution**, so its ceiling is the teacher — and 16 steps of distillation tops out at ~0.82–0.83. Pure RL is not teacher-bounded: gsm8k is small and **solvable from env reward**, so the policy climbs to the task ceiling (~1.0) on its own. A strong teacher doesn't help once the student can just solve the task. (Confirmed structurally by the OPD throughput grid: the **8B teacher fails the guard (0.578)** — a weaker teacher *lowers* the ceiling; teacher-size floor is >8B.)

**Mechanistic findings that fell out:**
- **GRPO lr knee = 1e-5**, two orders above OPD's distillation knee (3e-5). lr is the dominant lever in both, but the loss geometry differs.
- RL's near-ceiling result needs the **lr1e-5 × gen1024 combo** (neither alone clears 0.79) and an **entropy bonus** to avoid the collapse-to-0.04 that the bare lr1e-5 run shows. combo_acc_stab = ~0.95–0.98 *without* collapse.
- OPD is **93% teacher-forward-bound**; the only speed lever that paid is **top_k** (topk16 = 2.2× faster, lossless).

**Caveats — where this verdict does and doesn't hold:**
1. **Regime-specific.** gsm8k is small and saturable. The earlier MATH model-size sweep showed RL accuracy is *far* from ceiling at small sizes on harder math — on tasks the student **can't** solve from env reward alone, the 32B teacher signal (OPD) could still matter. This result is "small model, short-CoT, solvable task."
2. **Metric.** OPD pass@8 is a top-3-checkpoint mean; RL is last/peak. The ~0.94 vs ~0.82 gap dwarfs that difference, but they're not an identical estimator.
3. **OPD's biggest cost lever was never run.** Disaggregated teacher serving (teacher off the training GPUs) is deferred in the throughput grid — it would lower OPD's per-step cost, but it must close a ~10–20× gap to change the ranking, and it does nothing for the accuracy ceiling.

**Net:** for non-agentic gsm8k reasoning on Leonardo at this scale, **learning from env reward beats distilling a 32B teacher**, at lower compute. The open question OPD could still win is the harder-task / can't-solve-from-reward regime — that's the comparison worth running next, not another gsm8k pass.

## Next grids — the cross-designs (RL accuracy + OPD throughput)

The first two grids covered complementary corners: **RL** was a *throughput* sweep (sec/step, eff tok/s; reward unconverged at 25 steps, pass@8 never measured) and **OPD** was an *accuracy* sweep (pass@8 to ~0.75, but its speed cells ran at lr=1e-5 where nothing learned). To close the box — and to set up a clean controlled RL-vs-OPD head-to-head — here are the two complementary grids. Both run **to a real pass@8 readout** so the numbers are directly comparable across methods.

---

### Grid A — RL accuracy grid (gsm8k GRPO, Qwen2.5-1.5B, 1×4 A100-64GB)

**Goal:** the GRPO config that maximizes **gsm8k pass@8**, run **to a plateau** (not a 25-step probe). Metric = pass@8 (same eval harness as OPD) + **pass@8 per GPU-hour**; entropy/grad_norm as stability guard.

**Base = the throughput winner `combo_C`** (tbs128 · n8 · gmu0.85 · enforce_eager=false · micro16), 12,882 eff tok/s @ 20.7 s/step → ~175 steps/hr, so a to-convergence run fits an 8h wall easily. Raise `epochs` so wide-tbs cells don't exhaust the 7,473-row set before plateau.

**20 cells, 2 batches:**
- **Batch 1 — primary convergence levers (lr × group × CoT):** `base_long`, lr ∈ {3e-7, 1e-6, 3e-6, 1e-5, 3e-5} (re-find the GRPO knee — OPD's was 3e-5), n_samples ∈ {4, 16}, max_gen_len ∈ {1024, 2048}.
- **Batch 2 — stabilization + exploration + combos:** ref-KL {0.001, 0.01}, temperature {0.7, 1.2}, DAPO clip 0.28, entropy bonus, reward shaping (format/partial-credit), **`base_q3` = re-validate on Qwen3-1.7B** (OPD's student, for the head-to-head), then `combo_acc` (lr×n×gen winners) + `combo_acc_stab`.

> **Model-match note:** this grid inherits Qwen2.5-1.5B from the throughput base. For the apples-to-apples #6218 comparison the student should be **Qwen3-1.7B**; `base_q3` measures the rebase cost — decide before Batch 2.

Full plan (gist): https://gist.github.com/penfever/84faeb599d551625a93baaf7e2e99374

---

### Grid B — OPD throughput grid (Qwen3-32B teacher → Qwen3-1.7B student, gsm8k, 2×4 A100-64GB)

**Goal:** maximize OPD **throughput** (sec/step, steps/hr, **pass@8 per GPU-hour**) **while holding the converged accuracy** — re-optimize speed *around the accuracy optimum*, with **pass@8 ~0.75 as a HARD GUARD on every cell** (a cell that speeds up but drops pass@8 below ~0.70 is a *failed* speed cell).

**Base = the accuracy winner `combo_opt`** (lr3e-5 · top_k64 · n8 · gen1024 · teacher TP2 · colocated): pass@8 ~0.75–0.78, **832 s/step**. The bottleneck is known: OPD is **90–97% teacher-score-bound**, so throughput = cutting teacher-score cost without dropping pass@8. (The RL grid's gen/train levers are irrelevant here — student gen/train is <10% of the step.)

**20 cells, 2 batches:**
- **Batch 1 — teacher-serving + teacher-cost levers:** `base`, **`disagg`** (teacher on dedicated GPUs — biggest untapped lever, removes teacher↔student contention) + `disagg_mn`, teacher TP4, teacher FP8, teacher AWQ, **teacher size 14B / 8B** (the OPD-specific accuracy-vs-teacher-cost frontier), top_k ∈ {16, 32, 128} **re-validated @ lr3e-5** (the [OPD grid above](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6218#issuecomment-4643446059) found these flat — but at lr1e-5 where nothing learned).
- **Batch 2 — scored-token + efficiency + combos:** gen512, n4, sequence-packing / chunked teacher scoring, student gmu0.85, then `combo_fast` (disagg+fp8+topk32), `combo_cheap_teacher` (14b+topk32+n4), `combo_fast_mn`, `combo_balanced` (best pass@8-per-GPU-hour corner).

**Headline metric: pass@8 per GPU-hour** (computed in GPU-hours — disaggregation and smaller teachers change the denominator). The key deliverable is the **teacher-size↔pass@8 frontier**: how small a teacher still distills gsm8k to ~0.75.

Full plan (gist): https://gist.github.com/penfever/bcbe186b1638ba36676ecce0d702d05e

---

Together these produce, for both methods, **pass@8 + pass@8-per-GPU-hour at a converged operating point** on the same eval harness — exactly the controlled comparison recommended in the analysis above. `base_q3` (Grid A) + the existing OPD Qwen3-1.7B student make the head-to-head model-matched.

**Grid-B synthesis:** OPD is **93% teacher-forward-scoring-bound**, so **`top_k` is the only lever that paid** — **topk16 = 2.2× faster (387 vs 836 s/step) with pass@8 0.828 holding**. Disaggregation — the structurally biggest cost lever — was **not run**, so OPD's per-step floor here (~387 s/step) is not yet its best possible.

spillover_issues.body:
🤖
## Description
Follow-up to #6139 and related to #5328.

The current Grug ring EP path materializes global token/output buffers per rank. It all-gathers `x`, `selected_experts`, and `combine_weights`, gathers local expert assignments from `x_global`, then scatters into `out_global` before `psum_scatter` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py:38`, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py:91`, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py:110`). For small d2560/top-4 shapes this plumbing is a large fixed cost relative to expert math.

Add an assigned-token EP path that moves only routed assignments and produces the layout expected by `ragged_dot`: `x_dispatch`, assignment weights, return metadata, and local expert `group_sizes`. This can be a simpler single-node all-to-all/ragged path or a DeepEP handoff that avoids the extra local repack in `_pack_deepep_local_assignments` and `segment_sum` collapse (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py:50`, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py:88`).

### Definition of Done
- No per-rank `x_global` or `out_global` activation buffer is required for the new path.
- Forward and backward match existing ring EP top-k combine semantics.
- Add a perf smoke test on the issue6044 d2560 shape comparing ring EP vs the new assigned-token path.
- Keep local GMM kernel work separate from this issue unless needed for the dispatch contract.

# Research

Ring EP forces every shard to materialize `x_global` and `out_global` of shape `(tokens * ep_size, D)` even though each shard only consumes its local-expert slice. At d2560/top-4 the all-gather + scatter + `psum_scatter` plumbing dominates expert math. The two existing alternatives both pay extra cost: `ragged_all_to_all` uses a slow transport primitive on B200 (#6139 numbers), and the DeepEP path does a host repack (`_pack_deepep_local_assignments`) plus a `segment_sum` collapse before/after the GMM that an assignment-native contract would skip.

**Relevant code**
- [`ep_ring.py#L38-L40`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py#L38-L40) — three full all-gathers per call

- [`ep_deepep.py#L81-L97`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py#L81-L97) — `segment_sum` collapse before combine transport

# Proposed Approach (design change, needs review)

Add a fourth EP backend `assigned_token` selected via the existing implementation knob at [`grug_moe.py#L208-L215`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L208-L215). New file `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_assigned_token.py` exposes `_moe_mlp_ep_assigned_token_local(...)` with the same signature as the other three shard-local fns.

Dispatch contract: produce `(x_dispatch[TK_recv, D], assignment_weights[TK_recv], return_metadata, local_group_sizes[EL])` directly — the layout `ragged_dot` already consumes. No `x_global`, no `out_global`, no `segment_sum` collapse.

Sketch (shard-local, inside `shard_map("expert")`):

1. Per-shard expert-sorted permutation of routed assignments — reuse `_permute_by_global_expert` from `ep_common.py:44`. Each shard knows, for every global expert, how many of its own tokens land there.
2. Cross-shard sizing with one `all_gather` of the per-expert counts (small: `[num_experts]` int32, not `[tokens, D]` bf16). Derive `send_sizes` / `recv_sizes` for `ragged_all_to_all` of the routed-assignment payload — same shape calc as `ep_ragged_all_to_all.py:_shard_a2a_params` but built from per-edge counts so we never materialize `x_global`.
3. `ragged_all_to_all` of `(x_repeated_by_topk, combine_weight_repeated_by_topk)` into a receive buffer sized by `local_capacity = ceil(capacity_factor * assignments / ep_size)`. Capacity clipping reuses `_clip_receiver_group_sizes`.
4. Result is already grouped by local expert id → feed into `ragged_dot` directly (no `_pack_deepep_local_assignments` step).
5. Combine: multiply `out_dispatch` by `assignment_weights[:, None]` in place, then `ragged_all_to_all` with the transposed routing table back to the sender. On return, `_unpermute_from_global_expert` (already does the topk → token sum-combine) closes the loop.

Backward: the only custom-VJP-needing piece is the assignment permutation, which is already covered by `_sort_activations_custom` in `ep_common.py:17-31`. `ragged_all_to_all` has working autodiff on the existing path (`ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`), so reuse that.

Differences vs. `ragged_all_to_all` backend: that one keeps a per-shard `x_global`-equivalent (`sorted_x` with `assignments_per_shard` rows, then compacts via `keep_mask`). The proposed path sends only the post-capacity tail and removes the round-trip `_compact_by_keep_mask` / `_expand_from_keep_mask` pair.

Differences vs. `deepep`: skip `_pack_deepep_local_assignments` (the receive buffer is already grouped) and skip `_collapse_deepep_local_assignments` (weights applied on the dispatch side).

# Validation Plan

- Unit test in `lib/levanter/tests/grug/` parameterized over `(EL, ep_size, topk, capacity_factor)` that runs both `_moe_mlp_ep_ring_local` and the new fn under a CPU `shard_map` with a 4-device fake mesh and checks `allclose` on forward output and on the W13/W2 gradients. This is the DoD "fwd/bwd match ring EP" gate.
- Drop-counter parity: confirm `dropped_total` matches ring under low capacity.
- Perf smoke on d2560/top-4 from #6044 — separate `@pytest.mark.slow` benchmark that records ring vs assigned-token wall-time and prints the ratio. Not asserted; the artifact is what's reviewed.

# Open Questions

1. Is `jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all` differentiable on B200/TPU in the configurations Grug ships, or is the existing `ep_ragged_all_to_all` path relying on a workaround? If a custom VJP is needed, this becomes a 300+ LOC change rather than 150.
2. Should this share a file with `ep_ragged_all_to_all.py` (both use `ragged_all_to_all`) or stay separate for the perf-comparison story #6139 asks for?
3. Capacity model: ring uses `local_capacity = ceil(capacity_factor * tokens * topk / ep_size)`. The assigned-token path can either match that or use a tighter per-expert cap. Match ring exactly for the parity test, leave tuning for follow-up?

Estimated size: ~150-250 LOC new code + ~100 LOC test = above the 100-line auto-PR threshold, hence asking for review first.

spillover_issues.author: ClassicLarry
spillover_issues.body:
Add a Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) linear-attention path to the grug MoE model and interleave it ~3:1 with full softmax-attention layers, so long-context training/inference scales in compute and memory without the O(L^2) cost on every layer. The **primary success criterion is performant MFU on the KDA (linear-attention) layers** on GB200 (Blackwell SM100): a token-by-token recurrence is unusable, so the implementation uses the chunked-parallel delta-rule form (intra-chunk parallel matmuls + inter-chunk state recurrence), and must be SPMD-shardable across racks (no repeat of the FA4 device-0 failure mode).

## KDA algorithm
KDA (Kimi Linear, Moonshot) is the gated delta rule — DeltaNet with a data-dependent, **per-channel** forget gate. Per token, with recurrent state `S ∈ R^{d_k×d_v}`:

```
S_t = Diag(alpha_t) S_{t-1} + beta_t k_t (v_t - S_{t-1}^T k_t)^T
o_t = S_t^T q_t
```

- `alpha_t = exp(g_t) ∈ (0,1]^{d_k}` — per-channel decay (this fine-grained gate is what distinguishes KDA from scalar-gated Gated DeltaNet). `g_t = -exp(A_log)·softplus(low_rank(x)+dt_bias)`.
- `beta_t = sigmoid(...) ∈ (0,1)` — write strength.
- q,k are L2-normalized (eigenvalue stability of `I - beta k k^T`); q scaled by `1/sqrt(d_k)`.
- Output: RMSNorm + sigmoid gate + output projection.

Sources: Kimi Linear tech report (arXiv 2510.26692, KDA Eqs. 1–10), Gated Delta Networks (arXiv 2412.06464), Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule (arXiv 2406.06484), and `flash-linear-attention` (`fla/ops/kda/naive.py`, `fla/ops/gated_delta_rule/naive.py`).

## Chunked-parallel form (the MFU-critical piece)
Split length L into chunks of C=64. Per chunk, in fp32, with `b^r = cumsum(g)` per channel:
- Fold per-channel decay into q/k so all interactions are plain matmuls: `k_inflate = k·exp(b)`, `k_deflate = k·exp(-b)`, `q_inflate = q·exp(b)`.
- Delta-correction matrix `A[r,i] = -beta_r (k_inflate_r · k_deflate_i)` (strictly lower); invert unit-lower-triangular `(I - A)` by forward substitution → `T`.
- Pseudo-values `U = T (beta·V)`; decayed-key summary `k_cumdecay = T (beta·k·exp(b))`.
- Scan over chunks carrying `S`:
  `v_new = U - k_cumdecay·S`;
  `O = (q·exp(b))·S + Tril(q_inflate · k_deflate^T)·v_new`;
  `S <- Diag(exp(b^C)) S + (exp(b^C - b)·k)^T v_new`.

This is matmul-bound (C×C and C×d GEMMs) and pure JAX (no `custom_call`/callback), so XLA partitions it. It is a systematic per-channel broadening of the scalar `chunk_gated_delta_rule` already in-repo (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/layers/gated_deltanet.py`), which is validated against HF Qwen3-Next fwd+bwd (`lib/levanter/tests/test_gdn_kernels.py`) — we build/verify scalar-first, then broaden `g` to `[...,d_k]`.

## Hybrid layer schedule
Interleave ~3:1 KDA:full. Every `period`-th layer (default 4) plus the last is full causal softmax attention; the rest are KDA. This replaces the existing sliding/full schedule when the KDA hybrid is enabled; sliding window is dropped (KDA's decay + recurrent state provide local and global mixing). Kimi Linear uses head_dim 128, chunk 64, 3:1 ratio, NoPE on KDA layers.

## Integration plan
- `experiments/grug/moe/kda.py` (new): `recurrent_kda` (sequential reference) + `chunk_kda` (chunked-parallel), per-channel gate, batched over leading `(B,H)` dims.
- `experiments/grug/moe/model.py`:
  - `GrugModelConfig`: `kda_hybrid: bool`, `kda_full_attn_period: int`, `kda_chunk_size: int`.
  - `CausalSelfAttention`: add small decay/beta projections present on every layer (uniform pytree so the stacked `lax.scan` still works), used only on KDA layers; a KDA branch (no RoPE/XSA) that projects q/k/v, computes gates, runs `chunk_kda` under `shard_map`, applies output gate + `w_o`.
  - `Block.__call__`: `use_kda` flag selects softmax vs KDA.
  - Schedule extended to KDA-vs-full in both the unrolled and stacked-`lax.scan` paths (`cond` on an `is_kda` scan input, keeping the scan body uniform).
- `experiments/grug/moe/launch_cw_scale.py`: `SCALE_ATTN_IMPL=kda_hybrid` enables it; `SCALE_KDA_PERIOD` / `SCALE_KDA_CHUNK` tune it. These are config-build-time knobs, so no `dispatch.py` env-forwarding is needed.

## MFU plan
- Kernel: chunked-parallel pure-JAX (portable, XLA-partitionable, no callback), chunk 64. Consider a Pallas/Mosaic-GPU kernel only if the pure-JAX path leaves MFU on the table.
- Measure `throughput/mfu` from the grug trainer (wandb). Caveat: the analytic `lm_flops_per_token` counts full O(L^2) attention for every layer, so for KDA layers it over-counts and the reported hybrid MFU is a conservative lower bound; also compare tokens/sec/GPU of the hybrid vs the all-softmax baseline at matched config.
- Target: KDA-layer step time at or below the softmax layers it replaces at long seq (8k+), so the hybrid's tokens/sec/GPU exceeds the all-full-attention run.

## Sharding-safety requirement
The FA4 attention is bridged via `cutlass_call`→`jax.pure_callback`, which pins metadata to `{maximal device=0}` and breaks multi-rack SPMD (#7012, #6979). KDA must NOT reintroduce that: it is pure JAX and runs inside a `shard_map` over the batch axes (`replica_dcn,data,expert`) and head axis (`model`), with sequence/head_dim unsharded, so each device carries fully-local recurrent state with no collectives inside attention.

## Validation
- `chunk_kda` vs `recurrent_kda` (max-abs < 1e-4 fp32) across chunk sizes/shapes; scalar-limit cross-check vs levanter `recurrent_gated_delta_rule`.
- Tiny end-to-end grug fwd/bwd on CPU with `kda_hybrid=True`.
- Single-node GB200 MFU probe (shared cluster: check usage first, hold at most ~1 node/rack).
